question: Identify the artist with the highest overall sales of albums (tie broken by alphabetical order) and the artist with the lowest overall sales of albums (tie broken by alphabetical order), then calculate the amount each customer spent specifically on those two artists’ albums. Next, compute the average spending for the customers who purchased from the top-selling artist and the average spending for the customers who purchased from the lowest-selling artist, and finally return the absolute difference between these two averages.
sql:
WITH artist_sales AS (
    SELECT 
        al.ArtistId,
        ar.Name AS ArtistName,
        SUM(ii.UnitPrice * ii.Quantity) AS total_sales
    FROM invoice_items ii
    JOIN tracks t ON ii.TrackId = t.TrackId
    JOIN albums al ON t.AlbumId = al.AlbumId
    JOIN artists ar ON al.ArtistId = ar.ArtistId
    GROUP BY al.ArtistId, ar.Name
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT 
        ArtistId,
        ArtistName,
        total_sales,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY total_sales DESC, ArtistName ASC) AS rn_top,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY total_sales ASC, ArtistName ASC) AS rn_low
    FROM artist_sales
),
top_low AS (
    SELECT 
        MAX(CASE WHEN rn_top = 1 THEN ArtistId END) AS top_artist_id,
        MAX(CASE WHEN rn_top = 1 THEN ArtistName END) AS top_artist_name,
        MAX(CASE WHEN rn_low = 1 THEN ArtistId END) AS lowest_artist_id,
        MAX(CASE WHEN rn_low = 1 THEN ArtistName END) AS lowest_artist_name
    FROM ranked
),
customer_spending AS (
    SELECT 
        i.CustomerId,
        ar2.Name AS CustomerArtistName,
        ar2.ArtistId,
        SUM(ii.UnitPrice * ii.Quantity) AS spending
    FROM invoice_items ii
    JOIN tracks t ON ii.TrackId = t.TrackId
    JOIN albums al ON t.AlbumId = al.AlbumId
    JOIN artists ar2 ON al.ArtistId = ar2.ArtistId
    JOIN invoices i ON ii.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId
    WHERE ar2.ArtistId IN (
        (SELECT MAX(CASE WHEN rn_top = 1 THEN ArtistId END) FROM ranked),
        (SELECT MAX(CASE WHEN rn_low = 1 THEN ArtistId END) FROM ranked)
    )
    GROUP BY i.CustomerId, ar2.Name, ar2.ArtistId
),
top_avg AS (
    SELECT AVG(spending) AS avg_spending
    FROM customer_spending
    WHERE ArtistId = (SELECT MAX(CASE WHEN rn_top = 1 THEN ArtistId END) FROM ranked)
),
low_avg AS (
    SELECT AVG(spending) AS avg_spending
    FROM customer_spending
    WHERE ArtistId = (SELECT MAX(CASE WHEN rn_low = 1 THEN ArtistId END) FROM ranked)
)
SELECT 
    ta.avg_spending AS top_avg,
    la.avg_spending AS low_avg,
    ABS(ta.avg_spending - la.avg_spending) AS abs_diff
FROM top_avg ta, low_avg la
